clue.text: Flourish, fitting into Society? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: the clue's literal reading puts one piece inside the other, the word into marking the insertion
this swaps the roles the surface gives, so the word for fitting goes round the abbreviation instead of inside it

parts.note: fitting means proper, suitable

explanation.surface: A question of whether thriving means fitting in with polite society, answered with a dry contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'fitting into Society' puts PROPER inside S; 'Quite the reverse' flips that, so S goes inside PROPER.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish is to thrive and do well, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Controversial motorway splitting European state

indicators.note: splitting means the motorway cuts into the run of European and state

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway

explanation.surface: A divisive new motorway carving up a European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European state' reads as one country but is two separate pieces, with the motorway splitting them; 'splitting' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemical writing is argumentative and disputatious, so stirs controversy.

clue.text: Ishmael, say, not in form

parts.note: out means not in
a cast is a form or mould

explanation.surface: A character, Ishmael, out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Ishmael, son of Abraham and Hagar, was sent away into the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Ishmael was driven out of his family, so he is an example of a rejected exile.

clue.text: Picture by surreal photographer in grand opening

indicators.note: in places the photographer inside the grand opening

parts.note: a portal is an imposing doorway or gate
Man Ray was the American Surrealist photographer

explanation.surface: An image by a Surrealist photographer shown at a gala opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand opening' sounds like a launch event but is an imposing door, PORTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrayal is a depiction or representation, so a picture.

clue.text: Travelled on right lines

parts.note: an ode is a poem, some lines of verse

explanation.surface: A journey made on the proper rails.
explanation.definitionFit: Rode is the past tense of ride, so went on horseback or by vehicle.

clue.text: Coal fire started by logs initially

indicators.note: started by places the logs letter at the front of the word for fire
initially asks for the opening letter of the word logs

parts.note: to fire is to ignite, set alight

explanation.surface: A coal fire got going by first lighting some logs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'started by' tells you the L from 'logs initially' comes before IGNITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lignite is a soft brown coal, so it is a type of the fuel named.

clue.text: Disguised aliens met, possessing new features

indicators.note: possessing means the jumbled letters hold the abbreviation for new
disguised asks for the letters of aliens met to be dressed up in a different order

explanation.surface: Encountering aliens in disguise who turn out to have new faces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disguised' signals the rearrangement of the two words that follow it, and 'possessing' means that jumble holds the letter for new.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineaments are the distinctive lines of a face, its characteristics.

clue.text: From Nicaragua valuable fruit is exported

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words Nicaragua valuable

explanation.surface: A precious crop shipped out of Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'NicaraGUA VAluable'.
explanation.definitionFit: The guava is a tropical fruit, an example of the category.

clue.text: Greet, in turn, the whole number

indicators.note: turn asks for the letters of greet and in to be turned into another order

explanation.surface: Everyone greets in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' looks like a phrase meaning 'one after another', but 'in' is part of the letters and 'turn' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, with no fractional part: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Always poetic — that's weird

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A remark that perpetual verse is strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, so a synonym.

clue.text: Alter arrangement in time

indicators.note: arrangement asks for the letters of Alter to be put in a new order

explanation.surface: A promise to change the arrangement of something eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' signals that the five letters of ALTER are reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening in time, eventually, happens afterwards, so the adverb for subsequently fits.

clue.text: In Yorkshire, back the other Rose to trap players following on

indicators.note: to trap means the reversed colour encloses the rest of the wordplay
back tells you to read the colour of the rival county's rose from right to left

parts.note: Yorkshire's emblem is the white rose, so the other Rose is Lancashire's red one

indicators.note: following puts the word for players after on

parts.note: a cast is the set of players in a show

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire partisan urged to support Lancashire's rose and enforce the follow-on in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Wars of the Roses York's emblem was the white rose and Lancaster's the red. 'back' reverses the colour, and 'to trap' and 'following' place the rest. In cricket, 'follow on' makes the side batting second bat again.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is a locator: the answer is a town in South Yorkshire, home of a famous racecourse.

clue.text: Silver found in lake is paltry

indicators.note: found in places the symbol for silver inside the word for lake

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A disappointing haul of silver recovered from a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry and the answer both mean scanty, small in amount: synonyms.

clue.text: Eccentric dispute in French region

parts.note: an eccentric is a cam, an off-centre wheel in machinery
to dispute is to argue

explanation.surface: An oddball's quarrel taking place somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like an adjective but is a noun: in engineering an eccentric is a cam, giving CAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Camargue is the delta of the Rhône in southern France, known for its white horses.

clue.text: The kind of skill needed to produce Pinafore?

definitions.text: The kind of skill needed to produce Pinafore?

parts.words: The kind of skill needed to produce Pinafore
parts.note: read straight, the theatrical know-how for mounting Gilbert and Sullivan's opera; read again, HMS Pinafore is a ship, a boat built for the boards

explanation.surface: What it takes to put on a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera set aboard a ship, so the vessel itself is a craft of the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The theatrical skill of putting on plays, with a pun on a ship made for the theatre.

clue.text: Spiteful race in Caribbean island

indicators.note: in places the race's letters inside the word for an island

parts.note: a cay is a low islet or reef, especially in the Caribbean
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Nasty racial feeling on a West Indian island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' is not about ethnicity: it is the Isle of Man motorcycle race, and 'in' puts it inside the island word.
explanation.definitionFit: Catty describes remarks that are spiteful and malicious, a synonym.

clue.text: Financial controller making rate revision more certain

indicators.note: revision asks for the letters of rate to be reworked into a new order

parts.note: surer is the comparative of sure, meaning more certain

explanation.surface: An accountant who becomes more confident by revising the interest rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' rearranges RATE into TREA, followed by SURER.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer manages the funds of a club or organisation, so is its money controller.

clue.text: Tricky movement for rock bands to prize

parts.note: strata are layers or bands of rock
a gem is something prized, a treasure

explanation.surface: A rock group's clever chord change wins an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock bands' suggests musicians but means geological layers.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning plan or manoeuvre, a crafty move.

clue.text: Ambassador owing money is sent down

annotationWithheld.why: Ambassador owing money is sent down (9): the parse is LEGATE inside RED (in the red, owing money), so 'owing money' gives RED and also signals the containment, one phrase doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Ambassador owing money is sent down

clue.text: Illumination needed for backward degree student meeting difficulty

indicators.note: backward turns round the run made of degree and student together

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
L is a learner, from the L-plate
a plight is a difficult situation

explanation.surface: A struggling student needs a light to study by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns MA plus L into LAM, followed by PLIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamplight is the glow given by a lamp, a kind of illumination.

clue.text: Examine mounting in spy glass

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for spy

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted in an organisation

indicators.note: mounting, in a down clue, means the word for examine is read upwards

parts.note: to con is to study or examine closely

explanation.surface: A spyglass set up to examine something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spy glass' looks like a telescope, but 'spy' is MOLE and 'glass' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocle is a single eyeglass, so a glass in that sense.

clue.text: Rides booked by Cobbett were so countrified

definitions.text: Rides booked by Cobbett were so

explanation.surface: A note that the journeys William Cobbett wrote up were all in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: William Cobbett, an English radical journalist, published a book of countryside journeys on horseback in 1830 called Rural Rides.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobbett's book title pairs the word with Rides; and countrified means belonging to the countryside, not the town.

clue.text: Design apparent in cut of old dress.

indicators.note: apparent in says the aim is visible within the word for cut

parts.note: a rent is a tear or cut
a design is an aim, an intention

explanation.surface: A pattern visible in the cut of a vintage frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Design' and 'cut' suggest dressmaking, but they mean AIM and RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an archaic word for clothing, so dress of an old style of speech.

clue.text: Personally select worker and implement

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
a pick is a digging tool

explanation.surface: Choosing a labourer and a tool yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: To handpick is to choose carefully oneself, a synonym of personally select.

clue.text: "Cry ____ and let slip the dogs of war" (J Caesar)

definitions.text: "Cry ____ and let slip the dogs of war" (J Caesar)

parts.words: Cry ____ and let slip the dogs of war
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank: Mark Antony's line in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar has one word missing after Cry

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare quotation with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Antony's speech over Caesar's body in Julius Caesar, Act 3, gives the line; the blank is the word shouted to signal a sack.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the cry for unrestrained slaughter and plunder, meaning devastation.

clue.text: Brief heyday

explanation.surface: A two-word note that someone's best years were short.
explanation.definitionFit: To prime someone is to brief or prepare them; and one's prime is one's peak years.

clue.text: Run to take part in smart procession

indicators.note: to take part in puts the letter for run inside the word for smart

parts.note: to smart is to sting, as a wound does
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Jogging to join an elegant parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' looks like an adjective, elegant, but is the verb: to smart is to sting.
explanation.definitionFit: A string is a line of things one after another, as a procession of horses or people.

clue.text: Consummate ring performer

explanation.surface: Praise for a perfect circus act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consummate' looks like the adjective, perfect, but is the verb, complete.
explanation.definitionFit: To seal a deal is to complete it; and a trained sea mammal balancing balls is a circus ring act.

clue.text: Insure against illness for short holiday — at Nice, perhaps

parts.note: vac is short for vacation, a holiday

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of at Nice could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Getting jabs before a quick break on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals the rearrangement of the two words beside it. 'Insure' is used loosely here for 'protect in advance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inoculating someone protects them in advance against a disease, a loose sense of insure.

clue.text: Visitor intuitively identified by word of mouth

indicators.note: by word of mouth says the word for intuitively identified is heard, not read

parts.note: guessed means worked out by intuition

explanation.surface: Someone recognised by a hunch on the strength of hearsay.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is someone invited to stay or visit, a synonym of visitor.

clue.text: Fair investment of money in bond

indicators.note: investment of means clothing or surrounding, so the bond word wraps the money letter

parts.note: cement is a bond, something binding
L stands for the pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A just and sensible placing of cash in a bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' is used in its old sense of clothing or enclosing, so CEMENT goes round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather is mild and pleasant, which is what fair weather means.

clue.text: Very small sum included in cover is inadequate

indicators.note: included in puts the small sum inside the word for cover

parts.note: a lid is a cover
a mite is a tiny amount of money, as in the widow's mite

explanation.surface: Insurance cover with a tiny sum assured is not enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Limited means restricted in amount, so short of what is needed.
